puppet-augeasproviders_grub.acceptance_reason: GRUB providers are confined to specific hardware/boot scenarios; acceptance tests require reboot semantics and filesystem access incompatible with containerized environments. Module scope fundamentally conflicts with Docker/container-based testing.

puppet-elastic_stack.acceptance_reason: Previously recorded as blocked on the assumption it shared puppet-elasticsearch's vm.max_map_count/systemd/artifact-download blockers. It does not — its only acceptance suite is a single elastic_stack::repo idempotency test that manages a yum/apt repo definition, with no Elasticsearch service dependency. Enabled via GCP VM acceptance (docs/vm-based-acceptance-testing.md §7.4).

puppet-elasticsearch.acceptance_reason: Previously blocked on vm.max_map_count >= 262144 (a host kernel parameter an unprivileged Docker container can't set). Enabled via GCP VM acceptance using the vm_setup_commands capability (docs/vm-based-acceptance-testing.md §7.4/§7.6) to pre-set the sysctl and install wget (missing from the stock Rocky 9 GCP image; needed by this module's package_url install path to download the Elasticsearch package) over SSH as root before Beaker starts. Live-verified green on Rocky 9, 171/171 examples passing.

puppet-jira.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests exist upstream but are not yet wired into a harness setfile/target.

puppet-openldap.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests use Dir.mktmpdir on the Beaker controller to create temporary directories for LDAP database paths (olcDbDirectory), then reference those host-local paths inside the Docker SUT where they do not exist; slapd rejects them with "invalid path: Permission denied". The tests assume a shared controller/SUT filesystem (VM/Vagrant model). Requires VM-based Beaker or upstream test changes to create directories inside the SUT.

puppet-rsyslog.acceptance_reason: Blocked on two GCP images, neither a Puppet Core compatibility issue. Rocky 9: google-compute-engine hard-depends on rsyslog, blocking the module's own package-removal cleanup. Switching to debian-12 got past that but hit a different, real bug: rsyslog.service's Requires=syslog.socket resolves via its Alias=syslog.service name, which only exists while the unit is enabled — the suite's repeated package install/remove cycles intermittently disable it mid-run, breaking the socket trigger. Confirmed via Ubuntu 24.04's packaging that this is a Debian-family-wide rsyslog.service quirk, not an image choice, so switching images again wouldn't help. A start-rate-limit workaround was tried and had no effect. Needs an upstream/module-side fix, not a harness one.

puppet-selinux.acceptance_reason: Previously recorded as blocked because Docker/ubuntu-latest never loads the SELinux LSM. Enabled via GCP VM acceptance (docs/vm-based-acceptance-testing.md §7.5) on a real EL9 kernel, which does enforce SELinux. Upstream's own unmerged CI attempt (voxpupuli/puppet-selinux#399, run 25937845190) confirms the suite passes on EL9 (AlmaLinux 9, Rocky 9, CentOS 9, OracleLinux 9 all green there; only EL10 targets failed) once two master-branch bugs are patched — both applied here via pre_acceptance_commands rather than upstream: (1) spec/acceptance/class_disabled_spec.rb mixes let(:pp) and let(:manifest) across its three mode-switch contexts, so two of the three apply_manifest calls reference an undefined pp; (2) spec/acceptance/class_spec.rb declares an explicit selinux::fcontext/selinux::fcontext::equivalence resource pair and then also purges that same resource type in the same catalog. The suite reboots the host three times (class_disabled_spec.rb only); no harness-side reboot-tolerance capability was needed — Beaker's own Host#reboot already retries the SSH reconnect via net-ssh with a fibonacci backoff, independent of hypervisor.

puppet-systemd.acceptance_reason: Previously recorded as blocked because Docker's container runtime owns /etc/resolv.conf, breaking the module's symlink-replacement approach to managing it. Enabled via GCP VM acceptance (docs/vm-based-acceptance-testing.md §7.6) on Rocky 9, a real kernel where /etc/resolv.conf is not container-owned. Note: spec/acceptance/resolved_spec.rb only exercises manage_resolv_conf when the Beaker hypervisor is not container_podman — upstream's own green CI runs under container_podman and so has never actually exercised this path; this harness's hypervisor: none setfile does. A live run found one failure: the 'with mDNS enabled' context's resolvectl-status check never reports mDNS as active. Initially suspected SELinux (RHBZ#1430520-class denial); disproved by a live setenforce 0 test that changed nothing. Root cause is a GCP VPC networking limitation, not a guest-OS or Puppet Core issue — standard GCP VPC networks do not support multicast/broadcast at all (cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc), and mDNS is a multicast protocol by definition. Upstream's own CI never exercises this because it runs the identical systemd-resolved package inside a podman container on ordinary Docker bridge networking, which does support multicast. Patched via pre_acceptance_commands (same mechanism as puppet-selinux) to skip just that one assertion; the other 38 acceptance examples are real, valid Puppet Core coverage.

puppet-vault_lookup.acceptance_reason: Tests are purpose-built for Docker and self-contained, but use a three-container topology (certs.local, vault.local, puppetserver.local) that the single-SUT harness cannot orchestrate. The VaultDockerfile and PuppetserverDockerfile use multi-stage COPY --from=certs:latest builds the harness image-build pipeline does not support, and require a live Puppet Server (not puppet apply) with mTLS cert auth via a shared PKI. Requires harness-level support for multi-container nodesets and cross-image build dependencies.

puppet-wget.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests target only legacy OSes (Debian 8-9, Ubuntu 16.04-18.04, RHEL 6-7) — none of which match any available setfile — and hardcode `su - vagrant` to run puppet apply as a Vagrant user not present in Docker-based SUT containers. Requires new legacy setfiles or upstream test modernization.

puppet-windows_firewall.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests target Windows; the harness runs Linux Docker SUTs only. Requires Windows runner support.

puppet-windowsfeature.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests target Windows; the harness runs Linux Docker SUTs only. Requires Windows runner support.

treydock-puppet-kdump.acceptance_reason: Acceptance tests reboot the SUT and assert crashkernel appears in /proc/cmdline, set via the grub2 kernel_parameter provider (augeasproviders_grub). Docker SUTs share the host kernel cmdline (unchangeable from inside the container) and cannot reboot into a crashkernel-reserved kernel; kdump.service also requires boot-time crash-memory reservation. Same host-kernel/reboot blocker as its own augeasproviders_grub dependency. Requires a VM-based SUT.
